newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firm after late short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firm after late short-covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures scrambled to a new session high shortly before the close, buoyed by NYMEX led market-on-close buying, brokers said.

August Brent closed 33 cents up at $18.48 a barrel, having broken through resistance at $18.45, and touched a high of $18.57 in the last half hour of trade. July gas oil earlier closed up $1.50 a tonne at $165.25.

"We saw a late push at the end of the day, mainly led by (NYMEX crude). Some of the funds were trying to cover back their shorts...There's still a fair amount of shorts in the market although some of them have pushed their positions further down the board," a dealer said.
"We held above the recent high (at $18.45)...it's a strong settlement," said another.
The market's underlying strength was provided by comments made by Iraqi envoy Abdul Amir al-Anbari who said that he did not anticipate Baghdad resuming crude flows until August.
"It would take about a month for the new resolution to be implemented, including the oil sales," Anbari told Reuters in an interview in Geneva on Monday.
The market had foreseen an early to mid-July date after Iraqi oil minister Amir Muhammed Rasheed last week predicted quick agreement with the United Nations on an aid distribution plan.
Some pre-expiry buying on NYMEX products contracts had also earlier helped to support the oil complex, but gains were retraced and the contracts settled near session lows.
